messages:
Noah (Acme): Hey, our rerank calls started failing this morning after a deploy. Getting 410 / deprecated_model_id for model 'rerank-legacy-2021' and clients see empty scores. Can you help?

Jared (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste the request & response (sanitized) and a request-id or x-request-ts?

Noah (Acme): Sure. Example call:```POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "rerank-legacy-2021",
  "query": "Find best help articles",
  "candidates": ["A", "B", "C"]
}```Response: HTTP/1.1 410 Gone
{"error":"model_deprecated", "message":"model id rerank-legacy-2021 is deprecated", "request_id":"req_0a1b2c3d"}
Header: x-client-cache: v2

Priya (Support): Thanks — request_id req_0a1b2c3d received. Have you recently switched any tenant-scoped aliases or had a tenant migration?

Noah (Acme): We rotated keys and ran a deploy. No intentional alias changes. The client is customer-facing mobile app using an alias 'acme-ranker' that we thought points to the legacy model.

Jared (Support): Can you check the aliases mapping on your tenant? The platform can repoint an alias during rollout. From our side I'm checking audit logs.

rerank-bot: Audit entry: 1713000300 - alias acme-ranker repointed from rerank-legacy-2021 -> rerank-v2-2026 by deploy-bot (deploy-4821).

Noah (Acme): Wait, that would explain it — the new model expects a different input schema and we didn't update the client. But why 410 instead of a schema error?

Elena (ML Eng): Quick note: we return 410 when a model was decommissioned or explicitly deprecated. If an alias now points to a different model id that's active we return the new model id; 410 happens if the requested model id itself was soft-deleted. In your payload you passed a literal model id, not the alias?

Noah (Acme): Our mobile code uses the alias 'acme-ranker' (we thought). But the logs show the client resolves to literal id rerank-legacy-2021 cached in app storage. Looks like a client-side cache.

Priya (Support): Common pattern: client caches model id after alias resolve to avoid extra lookup. That cache can outlive server-side alias changes. Two mitigation options: 1) update clients to always call with alias (not cached id) or 2) server-side fallback mapping for recently deprecated ids.

Jared (Support): We've escalated to infra to add a short-lived redirect mapping for recently-deprecated rerank ids for the next 24h while you push a client update. Tracking: internal ticket INF-2198.

Noah (Acme): Appreciate that. Can you also provide repro steps so our mobile team can validate?

Elena (ML Eng): Repro steps: 1) In mobile debug console, clear any stored 'model_id' key. 2) Send a rerank POST using alias 'acme-ranker'. 3) Check response body for model id in metadata, e.g.,
```json
{ "model_used": "rerank-v2-2026", "scores": [...] }
```
If you still see 410 with literal id 'rerank-legacy-2021', capture the x-client-cache header and request_id and DM here.

Priya (Support): Also share the app version and exact SDK call. We suspect the SDK v1.4.2 wrote the model id into persistent storage. If so, upgrading to SDK v1.5.0 fixes alias-only usage.

Noah (Acme): Got it. Mobile team will push fix this afternoon. Thanks for the quick diagnosis. Any chance to surface a warning to tenants when an alias repoint may break clients?

Jared (Support): Good ask — filing product suggestion: PRD-742 to add alias-change notifications and a TTL for alias resolution caches. For now, INF-2198 will add the temporary redirect and I'll follow up when it's in place.

rerank-bot: INF-2198 created by Jared — temporary mapping applied (rerank-legacy-2021 -> rerank-v2-2026) expiring 1713087600.

Noah (Acme): Redirect confirmed working in our staging after clearing cache. Scores look sane again. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Elena (ML Eng): Follow-up: we'll schedule a postmortem doc to outline alias best-practices and SDK changes. Assigning to eng-ml for doc.

Priya (Support): Closing on our side once we see mobile rollout in prod. Please ping if anything else crops up.
